verdict.line: You lose if you facecheck his Shadow Dash range near his tower; you win if you poke in Cannon stance every time Feint is down.

brief.thesis: Shen has exactly one gap closer, E (Shadow Dash, 16/14/12/10/8s cooldown), and no other hard engage — if you track that cooldown and stay outside 575 range when it's up, Jayce's Cannon-stance poke wins the exchange every time. The measured numbers back this: Jayce holds the lane advantage and the solo-kill advantage here even though the raw head-to-head win rate (48.7% over 1342 games) sits close to even, because Shen's kit is built for roaming and teamfight utility, not for winning 1v1 trades.

theirWindow.when: Shadow Dash is up and you're overextended
theirWindow.what: Shen will dash in, taunt you, and chain Q (Vorpal Blade) autos to heal off you. Back out to minion range so the dash either whiffs or taunts you into a wave you can trade through, not into his tower.

yourWindow.what: Swap to Cannon stance, land Hyper Charge-boosted autos plus Shock Blast, and commit the full trade — he has no shield to eat the burst.

start.why: Run in 94.3% of games at 48.6% win rate — the extra sustain and early AD matter because you're going to be trading autos in Cannon stance from level 1.

boots.why: Taken in 39.5% of games at 49.2% win rate; the cooldown reduction shortens your Q and E windows, which is what actually punishes his Feint downtime.

core.why: Builds mana for Muramana scaling and keeps your Hammer-stance W (Lightning Field) mana-neutral during poke exchanges.
The highest-winrate path (50.9% over 116 games) runs this second — the active haste lets you reset range after a Shock Blast poke before he can close.
Converts your mana into the burst that actually wins trades once he's used Feint.

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards you for kiting after a trade, which is exactly the pattern you want against a champion whose only follow-up is a single-use dash on a long cooldown.

summoners.why: This page has the highest measured win rate (51%) in the matchup, and it matches the data: you hold the solo-kill advantage, so Ignite converts poke damage into kills instead of letting him walk away and heal it off with Q.

playing.title: Track Shadow Dash, not his HP bar
playing.detail: His E is on a real cooldown (16/14/12/10/8s) and it's his only taunt. If it's down, he physically cannot force a trade — walk up and poke freely.

playing.title: Poke from Cannon, finish from Hammer
playing.detail: Stay in Cannon stance for Hyper Charge-boosted autos and Shock Blast range; only swap to Hammer stance to knock him back with Thundering Blow or to dodge a committed Shadow Dash.

playing.title: Fire Shock Blast through your Acceleration Gate
playing.detail: Deploying E's gate and firing Q through it increases the missile's speed, range, and damage — use this to poke from further than his dash can reach.

playing.title: Bait Feint before you commit
playing.detail: Throw a single auto or Q first; if he pops W (Feint, 9/8/7/6/5s cd) to shield it, wait it out before unloading your real combo.

playing.title: Never stand in dash range near his tower
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to respect the taunt near his turret — a taunt there into tower shots is the one trade that actually loses you the lane.

playing.title: Deny his Ki Strike resets
playing.detail: His passive cooldown drops every time he hits a minion, monster, or champion. Don't let him free-farm the wave uncontested, or his empowered auto comes back faster than your trade timers.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade-window calls are my own read on the matchup, not measured stats.

stats.opponentTip: Deal damage constantly to gain lane control, but be careful of being taunted by Shen. Especially when you are under his turret.
